quote: I don't know. It didn't convince me.
stewart_read: Direct disclosure of a prior failed pitch; rep should have asked which company and why it didn't land.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged this out of setter scope and deferred detail to the closer, which is defensible but should be flagged in the handoff.
coaching_implication: Ask one follow-up ('what didn't work for you about it?') to capture competitive intel and hand it to the closer.

quote: Of course. Yeah. When's the when was the last time you looked into it?
stewart_read: Second touch on the same disclosure; rep pivots to timeline instead of the substance of the objection.
alternative_hypothesis: Timeline info (2-3 years ago) is itself useful context showing tech/pricing has changed, so this may be a partial, intentional redirect rather than a full miss.
coaching_implication: Combine timeline question with a substance question in the same breath to not lose the thread.

quote: So March to April, I used a 172 kilowatts per hour.
stewart_read: Customer hands over the first hard usage number and the rep files it silently, moving straight into asking for more months instead of reflecting any hook back.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be strategically holding all commentary until the full year of data is in so the flip lands with complete numbers — supported by the fact the rep asks for the full year immediately after.
coaching_implication: Even a quick 'that's a good chunk of usage, no wonder the bill's been climbing' keeps the customer emotionally engaged while he's doing the heavy lifting of pulling data.

quote: Awesome. No. Thank you so much. That's exactly what we're looking for.
stewart_read: After receiving a full year of usage data showing a clear winter/summer spike pattern, rep thanks him and moves straight to booking without ever anchoring the pain (e.g., referencing the $1,892 February peak) into the pitch.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be deliberately leaving the number-crunching and emotional framing for the closer's design walkthrough, consistent with setter_scope_discipline.
coaching_implication: A one-line callback to the peak month ('yeah, that February number is rough — that's exactly what we want to fix') would anchor pain without overstepping into closer content.

quote: you just have a credit score of at least 670.
stewart_read: Rep states the schema-correct 670 threshold (no drift), and customer clears it easily with an 800+ score.
coaching_implication: No action needed — clean execution of this qualifier.

quote: We'll shoot you a reminder text just to double check that time still works so we're not calling you out of the blue.
stewart_read: Rep completes most of button-up (recap, reminder text, number reconfirm) but never asks the explicit 'is that fair?' handshake or states the one-hour block / no-driving line, only briefly mentioning not driving mid-explanation of the follow-up call.
coaching_implication: Close with the literal handshake question after the recap to lock in the verbal commitment, per script.
